title: COMPUTE ROUNDED on PIC 9(7)V99 — hand-computed expected values land off-by-one
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. AVG-OFF-BY-ONE.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-TOTAL    PIC 9(7)V99.
       01  WS-COUNT    PIC 9(7).
       01  WS-AVG      PIC 9(7)V99.
      *> AVERAGE-SALARY paragraph from DEPTPAY (Phase 5 in-scope).
      *> Computes WS-AVG = WS-TOTAL / WS-COUNT with COBOL ROUNDED
      *> semantics: half-away-from-zero at the LSD of the receiving
      *> field. ON SIZE ERROR falls through to ZERO so a divide-by-
      *> zero or overflow short-circuits without crashing.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       AVERAGE-SALARY.
           IF WS-COUNT = 0
              MOVE 0 TO WS-AVG
           ELSE
              COMPUTE WS-AVG ROUNDED = WS-TOTAL / WS-COUNT
                 ON SIZE ERROR MOVE 0 TO WS-AVG
              END-COMPUTE
           END-IF.
notes:
This is the trap PayrollEquivalence.cs surfaced live: the
Phase 5.4 PayrollServiceTest fixture asserts 5848.06 for
(111111.11 / 19) -- mathematically wrong; the correct
HALF_UP scale-2 result is 5847.95. The extract pipeline
must capture the ROUNDED + scale-2 semantic AND surface
the SME open question 'have the test fixture's expected
values been cross-checked?'. The harness then drives the
GnuCOBOL sidecar with the canonicalInputs above and
asserts row-for-row match against the in-process C# decimal
reference, which is what made the off-by-one visible.
